issue.title: Connection is dropped with MobaXTerm client
issue.body:

When connecting to ssh-mitm from MobaXTerm client version 21.5, the connection is dropped.

**To Reproduce**

1. Go to https://mobaxterm.mobatek.net/download-home-edition.html
2. Download and run MobaXterm Portable v21.5
3. Create new session to ssh-mitm and try to connect
4. Connection is dropped

body: Is there any update on this? The latest Ubuntu release (jammy, 22.04) includes version 2.9.3, so I think a lot of people are going to encounter this problem in the near future...and setting disabled_algorithm doesn't seem very user-friendly or, in some cases, even possible, if paramiko is used internally with some bigger python app.

A rewrite of the key authentication logic is on @bitprophet's roadmap, which IIUC would make all of the `disabled_algorithms` awkwardness unnecessary. (I know he very much dislikes the whole `disabled_algorithms` two-step, but it was the least-worst quick fix for some recent problems.)

Unfortunately, AFAIK there's no specific timeline for this rewrite (other things are higher priority; plus, @bitprophet has to balance paramiko with invoke and fabric in his OSS time), so downstream projects may just need to figure out how to cope with the `disabled_algorithms` interface for now. :-/

This was handled in #2017 but figured I'd add my below findings after @bitprophet 's bugfix. Didn't want to create a new issue since this one was still open.

Issue persists on OpenSSH 5.3. This is the latest version available for CentOS/CloudLinux 6 servers. This openssh version only offers "ssh-rsa" and the code that was implemented is explicitly looking for the "ssh-rsa-cert-v01@openssh.com" key type.

**paramiko debug**:
```DEBUG:paramiko.transport:Finalizing pubkey algorithm for key of type 'ssh-rsa'
DEBUG:paramiko.transport:Finalizing pubkey algorithm for key of type 'ssh-rsa'
DEBUG:paramiko.transport:Our pubkey algorithm list: ['rsa-sha2-512', 'rsa-sha2-256', 'ssh-rsa']
DEBUG:paramiko.transport:Server did not send a server-sig-algs list; defaulting to our first preferred algo ('rsa-sha2-512')
DEBUG:paramiko.transport:NOTE: you may use the 'disabled_algorithms' SSHClient/Transport init kwarg to disable that or other algorithms if your server does not support them!
INFO:paramiko.transport:Authentication (publickey) failed.
```

**sshd log**:
```
sshd[177383]: userauth_pubkey: unsupported public key algorithm: rsa-sha2-512
```

With OpenSSH_5.3 it doesn't work with 512 / 256 so if you try to disable them the preferred becomes ssh-rsa.
```
DEB [20221107-09:51:10.980] thr=5   paramiko.transport: Remote version/idstring: SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_5.3
INF [20221107-09:51:10.982] thr=5   paramiko.transport: Connected (version 2.0, client OpenSSH_5.3)
DEB [20221107-09:51:10.984] thr=5   paramiko.transport: === Key exchange possibilities ===
DEB [20221107-09:51:10.986] thr=5   paramiko.transport: kex algos: diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256, diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha1, diffie-hellman-group14-sha1, diffie-hellman-group1-sha1
DEB [20221107-09:51:10.987] thr=5   paramiko.transport: server key: ssh-rsa, ssh-dss
DEB [20221107-09:51:11.141] thr=5   paramiko.transport: Our pubkey algorithm list: ['rsa-sha2-512', 'rsa-sha2-256', 'ssh-rsa']
DEB [20221107-09:51:11.145] thr=5   paramiko.transport: Server did not send a server-sig-algs list; defaulting to our first preferred algo ('rsa-sha2-512')
DEB [20221107-09:51:11.146] thr=5   paramiko.transport: NOTE: you may use the 'disabled_algorithms' SSHClient/Transport init kwarg to disable that or other algorithms if your server does not support them!
```


Unfortunately, you then might run into an issue where OpenSSH_7.4 only accepts 512/256 but we have disabled them. 
So I ended up overriding paramiko.transport.Transport._preferred_pubkeys and reordering it to use ssh-rsa first.

Could the fix be to use paramiko.transport: server key (server_key_algo_list) to filter the list when server-sig-algs is not available instead of just defaulting to the [0] assuming auth_handler can access it from transport?
something like pubkey_algo = list(filter(server_key_algo_list, my_algos))[0]
``` else:
            # Fallback: first one in our (possibly tweaked by caller) list
            pubkey_algo = my_algos[0]
            msg = "Server did not send a server-sig-algs list; defaulting to our first preferred algo ({!r})"  # noqa
            self._log(DEBUG, msg.format(pubkey_algo))
            self._log(
                DEBUG,
                "NOTE: you may use the 'disabled_algorithms' SSHClient/Transport init kwarg to disable that or other algorithms if your server does not support them!",  # noqa
            )
```
```

DEB [20221107-09:30:40.624] thr=2   paramiko.transport: Local version/idstring: SSH-2.0-paramiko_2.11.0
DEB [20221107-09:30:40.704] thr=2   paramiko.transport: Remote version/idstring: SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_7.4
INF [20221107-09:30:40.705] thr=2   paramiko.transport: Connected (version 2.0, client OpenSSH_7.4)
DEB [20221107-09:30:40.777] thr=2   paramiko.transport: === Key exchange possibilities ===
...
DEB [20221107-09:30:40.901] thr=2   paramiko.transport: Switch to new keys ...
DEB [20221107-09:30:40.902] thr=2   paramiko.transport: Got EXT_INFO: {'server-sig-algs': b'rsa-sha2-256,rsa-sha2-512'}
DEB [20221107-09:30:40.902] thr=3   paramiko.transport: Attempting public-key auth...
DEB [20221107-09:30:41.084] thr=2   paramiko.transport: userauth is OK
DEB [20221107-09:30:41.086] thr=2   paramiko.transport: Finalizing pubkey algorithm for key of type 'ssh-rsa'

ERR [20221107-09:30:41.089] thr=2   paramiko.transport: Exception (client): Unable to agree on a pubkey algorithm for signing a 'ssh-rsa' key!
```

issue.title: paramiko.ssh_exception.SSHException: Invalid key

repository.name: paramiko
repository.description: The leading native Python SSHv2 protocol library.

license.name: GNU Lesser General Public License v2.1

issue.body:
Running Paramiko 3.2.0 under Python 3.9.13 and I am struggling to authenticate to a Cisco device using a password protected OpenSSH based RSA 2048 key. I was trying to get Ansible working using the `net_put` module, but it was failing with `No existing session` error, so I went back to basics and tried with the following simple Python script:

```
import paramiko

client = paramiko.SSHClient()
client.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.AutoAddPolicy())
client.connect('<IP>', username='ansible', passphrase='<KEY_PASSWORD>', key_filename="/home/ansible/.ssh/ansible/ansible_rsa2048", allow_agent=False, look_for_keys=False, timeout=10)
```

This results in the following (some lines excluded for brevity):

```
DEBUG:paramiko.transport:starting thread (client mode): 0xf4ce47f0
DEBUG:paramiko.transport:Local version/idstring: SSH-2.0-paramiko_3.2.0
DEBUG:paramiko.transport:Remote version/idstring: SSH-2.0-Cisco-1.25
INFO:paramiko.transport:Connected (version 2.0, client Cisco-1.25)
DEBUG:paramiko.transport:Trying discovered key b'45c7f2561309bbe78927141a6c4864e9' in /home/ansible/.ssh/ansible/ansible_rsa2048
DEBUG:paramiko.transport:userauth is OK
INFO:paramiko.transport:Authentication (publickey) failed.
DEBUG:paramiko.transport:Trying discovered key b'08278851e5fccacd788300e519db8760' in /home/ansible/.ssh/ansible/ansible_rsa2048
INFO:paramiko.transport:Disconnect (code 2): Protocol error: expected packet type 50, got 5
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/ansible/itpc/./x.py", line 12, in <module>
    client.connect('<IP>', username='ansible', passphrase='<KEY_PASSWORD>', key_filename="/home/ansible/.ssh/ansible/ansible_rsa2048", allow_agent=False, look_for_keys=False, timeout=10)
  File "/home/ansible/itpc/python/lib64/python3.9/site-packages/paramiko/client.py", line 485, in connect
    self._auth(
  File "/home/ansible/itpc/python/lib64/python3.9/site-packages/paramiko/client.py", line 818, in _auth
    raise saved_exception
  File "/home/ansible/itpc/python/lib64/python3.9/site-packages/paramiko/client.py", line 730, in _auth
    key = self._key_from_filepath(
  File "/home/ansible/itpc/python/lib64/python3.9/site-packages/paramiko/client.py", line 638, in _key_from_filepath
    key = klass.from_private_key_file(key_path, password)
  File "/home/ansible/itpc/python/lib64/python3.9/site-packages/paramiko/pkey.py", line 421, in from_private_key_file
    key = cls(filename=filename, password=password)
  File "/home/ansible/itpc/python/lib64/python3.9/site-packages/paramiko/ed25519key.py", line 65, in __init__
    signing_key = self._parse_signing_key_data(data, password)
  File "/home/ansible/itpc/python/lib64/python3.9/site-packages/paramiko/ed25519key.py", line 114, in _parse_signing_key_data
    raise SSHException("Invalid key")
paramiko.ssh_exception.SSHException: Invalid key
```

I don't understand why it is discovering two different keys in my keyfile - it was created with `ssh-keygen -b 2048 -t rsa`. I know the key is good as it works perfectly fine if I use OpenSSH:

```
$ ssh -i /home/ansible/.ssh/ansible/ansible_rsa2048 ansible@<IP>
Enter passphrase for key '/home/ansible/.ssh/ansible/ansible_rsa2048':

<IP>#
```

If I drop Paramiko down to 2.8.1 then it works perfectly fine (it also fixes my `net_put` Ansible issue) - I have tested numerous releases and it seems that it has been broken from 2.9.0 onwards

```
DEBUG:paramiko.transport:Local version/idstring: SSH-2.0-paramiko_2.8.1
DEBUG:paramiko.transport:Remote version/idstring: SSH-2.0-Cisco-1.25
INFO:paramiko.transport:Connected (version 2.0, client Cisco-1.25)
DEBUG:paramiko.transport:Trying discovered key b'45c7f2561309bbe78927141a6c4864e9' in /home/ansible/.ssh/ansible/ansible_rsa2048
DEBUG:paramiko.transport:userauth is OK
INFO:paramiko.transport:Authentication (publickey) successful!
```

body: I just ran into this problem connecting to a IOS-Xe 16.12.12 device with ssh-rsa key auth, and moved the order of pubkey algos in transport.py so ssh-rsa was before rsa-ssh2-512 and that fixed it for me.  openssh on RHEL9 doesn't have a problem picking the right pubkey algo FWIW.
